rounds.text: Jindal Capital Ltd is trading at a notable discount to its intrinsic value, offering a 24.1% margin of safety based on discounted cash flow calculations that put fair value at Rs 42 against a market price of Rs 32.1 [E42, E43]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price only prices in a modest 14.2% earnings growth rate, which falls well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E44]. This valuation disconnect occurs against a backdrop of exceptional profit acceleration, highlighted by a 54% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 96% growth over three years [E21, E20]. Operational quality is equally robust, supported by a superior return on assets of 4.5% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.94% [E8], alongside pristine cash conversion where March 2026 operating cash flow of Rs 1.86 Cr fully backs reported profits at a 1.65x ratio [E34, E35]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the past five years has contracted by 8% [E15]. Nevertheless, recent top-line momentum has decisively turned the corner with trailing twelve-month sales growth reaching 27% [E17], and operating margins expanding by 9 percentage points to 60% [E30], signalling that the business is primed for a major upward re-rating.

Jindal Capital Ltd exhibits persistent top-line contraction, with compounded sales growth over 10, 5, and 3 years negative at -9%, -8%, and -7% respectively [E14, E15, E16]. This long-term revenue decline is underscored by a flagged 5-year poor sales growth rate of -7.61% [E50] and an earnings profile that screens as cyclical [E47]. Valuation multiples appear unsupported given that the stock trades at a P/E of 31x and 26.38x against a sector benchmark of 19.16x [E1, E6], while commanding a price-to-book ratio of 3.18x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.25x [E7] and a book value multiple flagged explicitly as a negative [E48]. Furthermore, leverage risks are pronounced as debt-to-equity stands at 1.16x, meaning debt exceeds net worth after borrowings nearly doubled to ₹ 14.24 Cr in March 2026 from ₹ 7.76 Cr a year prior [E37, E38]. Shareholder returns are further compromised by a 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E4] and a low 3-year return on equity of 11.5% [E51].

Conceded: long-term compounded sales growth has contracted over 10, 5, and 3 years [E14, E15, E16, E50]. However, the bear ignores the dramatic inflection in recent results, where trailing twelve month sales growth has surged by 27% [E17] and screen reasons highlight a 40% year-over-year jump in sales [E53]. While the bear flags valuation multiples, the business compensates with superior profitability, boasting an ROA of 4.5% versus a sector benchmark of 1.94% [E8] and an ROE of 9.24% outperforming the sector's 5.13% [E9]. Furthermore, the bear's concern over valuation overlooks the disciplined DCF model which indicates a fundamental intrinsic value of Rs 42 per share, leaving a margin of safety of 24.1% [E42, E43]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but this retention fuels profit growth, evidenced by a 96% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E20], a 54% jump in trailing twelve month profits [E21], and operating cash flow fully backing reported profit at 1.65x [E34]. Finally, the bear's focus on debt ignores the strong cash generation of Rs 1.86 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E36], proving the business is actively outperforming stale sentiment [E59].

Conceded: trailing twelve month sales growth surged by 27% [E17] and screen reasons highlight a 40% year-over-year jump in sales [E53]. However, this short-term burst masks a severe structural contraction, characterized by compounded sales growth of -9% over 10 years, -8% over 5 years, and -7% over 3 years [E14, E15, E16, E50]. Furthermore, the bull's focus on superior profitability metrics like ROA [E8] and ROE [E9] ignores the company's low median return on equity of 5% over 10 years and 9% over 5 years [E26, E27], alongside an explicit rule-based screen flag for a low return on equity of 11.5% over the last 3 years [E51]. Conceded: a DCF model indicates a fundamental intrinsic value of Rs 42 per share [E42, E43]. Yet, this valuation optimism rests on an earnings growth assumption of 18.0% that exceeds the 14.2% already implied by today's price [E44], while screen reasons explicitly flag that earnings growth is decelerating [E57]. Finally, while the bull minimizes debt by citing free cash flow of Rs 1.86 Cr [E36], borrowings nearly doubled from Rs 7.76 Cr to Rs 14.24 Cr in March 2026 [E38], driving debt to equity to 1.16x where debt exceeds net worth [E37], and the yearly operating-margin trend remains inconsistent [E32].
